children.label: Estimated Federal Unobligated
children.help_text:
Lines 1-4, Columns (c) through (g)

For new applications, leave Column (c) and (d) blank. For each line entry in Columns (a) and (b), enter in Columns (e), (f), and (g) the appropriate amounts of funds needed to support the project for the first funding period (usually a year).

For continuing grant program applications, submit these forms before the end of each funding period as required by the grantor agency. Enter in Columns (c) and (d) the estimated amounts of funds which will remain unobligated at the end of the grant funding period only if the Federal grantor agency instructions provide for this. Otherwise, leave these columns blank. Enter in columns (e) and (f) the amounts of funds needed for the upcoming period. The amount(s) in Column (g) should be the sum of amounts in Columns (e) and (f).

For supplemental grants and changes to existing grants, do not use Columns (c) and (d). Enter in Column (e) the amount of the increase or decrease of Federal funds and enter in Column (f) the amount of the increase or decrease of non-Federal funds. In Column (g) enter the new total budgeted amount (Federal and non-Federal) which includes the total previous authorized budgeted amounts plus or minus, as appropriate, the amounts shown in Columns (e) and (f). The amount(s) in Column (g) should not equal the sum of amounts in Columns (e) and (f).

notes: Plan-first review proposal for FID241 v1.0; no compiled form or executable calculations are included.

Four independent arrays propose separate section ownership for A, B, C and E. Current SGG instead nests those sections in activity_line_items[], sharing the A/B activity title and allowing distinct C/E grant_program answers. Both approaches support C/E title overrides; separate lists are a design proposal, not a source requirement. Each DAT cell remains explicitly bound to its section index. Section B proposes activity-first navigation following the DAT tab-order instruction.

Section C and E activity titles default from the corresponding section A row but may be overwritten (DAT C-1-1…C-4-1 and E-1-1…E-4-1). They are distinct answers; SGG already preserves this distinction using grant_program within each section. Section B title forwarding remains a source-population obligation.

DAT business rules require an entry somewhere on the form except A-1-7…A-4-7, C-1-1…C-4-1 and E-1-1…E-4-1. On submission, blank activity titles become N/A according to the row-specific rule. These cross-field/submission rules are not represented as unconditional required fields.

Amounts are signed decimals. The imported Global-V1.0 DecimalMin1Max14Places2Type has totalDigits14 and fractionDigits2. multipleOf0.01 records precision; the harness does not certify totalDigits or a JavaScript-number representation. Decide numeric representation and boundary tests before implementation.

Preserve the DAT numeric value bounds, including its different negative minima for editable amounts (-99999999999.99) and many calculated outputs (-999999999999.99), with maximum999999999999.99. The XSD only limits totalDigits14/fractionDigits2; these stricter DAT bounds are individually recorded source discrepancies for review, not silently broadened.

Preserve each DAT field's population and overwrite rules. Section A activity new/revised totals (A-1-7 through A-4-7) are calculated defaults that may be overwritten, including for supplemental grants and changes to existing awards. Totals explicitly marked Calculated, read-only remain generated outputs. Keep the source formulas and validation messages for sections A through E; optionality in XSD does not decide editability or ownership.

Wire assembly must supply glob:FormVersionIdentifier for edition1.0, fixed programType Non-Construction and fixed coreSchemaVersion1.0. These are document metadata/constants, not additional applicant questions. The XSD schema version is1.0; its instance FormVersionIdentifier is not fixed by XSD.

Contextual field labels replace PDF-dependent row numbers, dollar signs and column positions. Every differing source value is recorded individually for review; this is a proposed presentation choice, not approval.

Current SGG comparison: api/src/form_schema/forms/sf424a/1/0/form_json.py and its validation/XML tests at HHS main1858f9a6. SGG uses decimal strings, shared activity rows, conditional title requirements, a completion confirmation and specialized budget widgets. DAT/XSD source agreement does not establish parity with those application behaviors. See forms/docs/sf424a-plan-review.md for the full answer-path mapping.

The Data tab contains authored illustrative answers before any TypeSpec definition exists. Money is shown as decimal strings, following SGG to avoid binary floating point rounding; exact representation, DAT bounds and arithmetic still need implementation validation. These samples are not emitted schemas or validated submissions.

DAT B-00-3 through B-00-6 also describe overwritable program titles, while current SGG shares activity_line_items[].activity_title between A and B. This is a concrete source-versus-existing-behavior question, not a casing or layout difference. The plan preserves separate answers pending explicit reconciliation.
description: Budget summary, cost categories, non-federal resources, cash needs, future funding and budget explanations. Four activity rows in each section retain their distinct source meaning; calculated outputs and defaults are explicit planning obligations.
risks: Existing SGG is the compatibility baseline. Reconcile the separate section lists against activity_line_items[] before TypeSpec. SGG shares the A/B title, but DAT B-00-3 through B-00-6 say section B titles may be overwritten. Resolve that source-versus-SGG conflict explicitly rather than silently coupling distinct source answers; also verify conditional requirements, completion behavior, calculated values and layout.
Review the proposed section/array boundaries and label context with Billy before form definition work.
Confirm the cross-field minimum-entry and N/A-on-submission rules, calculation ownership and rounding in implementation; static comparison cannot execute them.
Do not reuse a non-negative currency question without preserving signed values and the source totalDigits14/fractionDigits2 constraints.
Finite DAT slot annotations and explicit XSD-root selection are a proposed extension to the maintained review harness and require architectural review.
